author: Elastic
rule.description:
Detects `esxcli vm process list` on an ESXi host. The command lists running virtual machines and the world IDs of
their `vmx` processes. Those IDs are what a later kill command uses to stop the VMs and release the locks on their
virtual disks.
false_positives:
Administrators list virtual machines during maintenance and troubleshooting. Review whether the same session
then kills those processes or searches the datastore.
rule.name: ESXi Virtual Machine Process List
rule.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating ESXi Virtual Machine Process List

esxcli vm process list enumerates running virtual machines and their world ids. A later kill command uses those world ids to stop the VMs.

#### Possible investigation steps

- Read message for a plain list versus a list piped into vm process kill.
- Check the same session for pkill, power.off, snapshot removal, or a search for vmdk files.
- Confirm with the virtualization owner whether the list was part of a scheduled check.

### False positive analysis

A standalone list during a change window is commonly benign. A list immediately followed by a force kill of every world id is the shutdown step before encryption.

### Response and remediation

- If the same session kills virtual machines or deletes snapshots, isolate the host.
- Otherwise record the account and source for hunting on other hosts.
rule.setup:
## Setup

This rule requires ESXi host logs collected by the Elastic vSphere integration: https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/integrations/vsphere
rule.query: data_stream.dataset: "vsphere.log" and event.module: "vsphere" and message: ("esxcli" and "vm process list")
